title: What Are the Ukrainian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person (2026-11-05): corrected refresh target. Publish method: update in place, change slug and path to /expert-advice/ukrainian-wedding-traditions, confirm 301. /7-wedding-superstitions-you-need-to-check-off was given in error; keep it live and link it to the new article.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page in full with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch (retry with a render wait if no body); SEO pulls its ranked keywords (US and AU) and checks weddedwonderland.com for other Ukrainian or superstition pages. Keep any sourceable Ukrainian traditions; never reuse wording; drop errors.

Culture, not politics: no commentary on the war beyond Smartraveller's travel advice; respectful, warm tone. Ukrainian customs kept in Ukraine and the diaspora, including Australia; regional differences only where sourced.

Likely customs (brief finalises): svatannia (matchmaking) and the rushnyky given to the matchmakers; zaruchyny (engagement); divych vechir (the bride's evening) and the vinok (wreath); korovai (wedding bread) and its baking; the vykup (bride's ransom) as light play; the church wedding with the couple stepping onto a rushnyk, crowning in Orthodox and Greek Catholic rites; the welcome with bread and salt; the vesillia celebration, music and dances (hopak only where sourced). UNESCO: only elements whose own text links them to weddings (e.g. Cossack songs of Dnipropetrovsk region 2016, Petrykivka decorative painting 2013, Kosiv painted ceramics 2019, Ornamentation of Ukrainian vyshyvanka or other listings only if the page is confirmed live and the title matches). Ukrainian terms transliterated as sources give them.

Destination angle: Smartraveller Ukraine checked live. If 'Do not travel' (expected), never suggest marrying in Ukraine; the angle is Ukrainian-Australian and mixed-heritage couples bringing these customs to weddings elsewhere (Australia and other destinations), through Ukrainian Catholic and Orthodox parishes in Australia ('ask your parish priest'). Legal: only Smartraveller's own lines (dual nationals, consular help) and Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' on recognition; no claims about Ukrainian marriage law.

Sources: UNESCO, Ukrainian Catholic or Orthodox church official pages (including in Australia), Ukrainian museums and culture institutions, Britannica, encyclopaedias (Internet Encyclopedia of Ukraine, encyclopediaofukraine.com), academic sources. Unsourced becomes 'often told' with no meanings as fact and no [[VERIFY]] marker. One honest framing line per section.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (korovai, embroidered rushnyk) labelled illustrative pending approval; no images set in Ukraine; old-page images only if licence confirmed.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence must be a number; must_include_coverage entries must be objects with covered_by as an array; no extra sourcing rounds.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
